questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.explanation: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney; it includes the glomerulus, tubules and collecting system.

questions.q: The mitral (bicuspid) valve is located between the:
questions.explanation: The mitral valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle.

questions.q: Which cranial nerve is responsible for most eye movements, pupil constriction and eyelid elevation?
questions.explanation: CN III (oculomotor) innervates most extraocular muscles, the levator palpebrae and the pupil constrictor.

questions.q: The left ventricle has a thicker wall than the right ventricle because it:
options: Pumps blood against higher systemic resistance
Pumps blood only to the lungs
questions.explanation: Systemic vascular resistance is much higher than pulmonary resistance, so the left ventricle needs greater muscle mass.

questions.q: Which bone forms the forehead and the superior part of the orbits?
questions.explanation: The frontal bone forms the forehead and the roofs of the orbits.

questions.q: The diaphragm is primarily innervated by which nerve?
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve (C3–C5) is the main motor supply to the diaphragm.

questions.q: Which structure separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is the muscular partition between the thorax and abdomen.

questions.q: The pacemaker of the heart is normally the:
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node initiates the normal cardiac impulse.

questions.q: Which chamber of the heart receives deoxygenated blood from the systemic circulation?
questions.explanation: The right atrium receives venous blood via the superior and inferior vena cava.

questions.q: The tricuspid valve lies between the:
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve is the atrioventricular valve on the right side of the heart.

questions.q: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movement, balance and posture.

questions.q: Cranial nerve X is the:
questions.explanation: CN X is the vagus nerve; it has extensive parasympathetic supply to thoracic and abdominal organs.

questions.q: The largest organ of the body is the:
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight.

questions.q: Which cells produce myelin in the central nervous system?
questions.explanation: Oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons; Schwann cells myelinate peripheral nerves.

questions.q: The foramen magnum is found in which bone?
questions.explanation: The foramen magnum is the large opening in the occipital bone through which the spinal cord passes.

questions.q: Which valve prevents backflow of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle?
questions.explanation: The aortic valve closes during diastole to prevent aortic blood from returning to the left ventricle.

questions.q: The primary site of gas exchange in the lungs is the:
questions.explanation: Alveoli provide the large surface area and thin barrier needed for gas exchange.

questions.q: Which endocrine gland is located in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland sits in the sella turcica.

questions.q: The liver receives oxygenated blood mainly via the:
questions.explanation: The hepatic artery supplies oxygenated blood; the portal vein brings nutrient-rich blood from the gut.

questions.q: Which structure carries urine from the kidney to the bladder?
questions.explanation: The ureters transport urine from the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder.

questions.q: The atlas (C1) articulates superiorly with the:
questions.explanation: The atlas articulates with the occipital condyles, allowing nodding movements.

questions.q: Which muscle is the primary muscle of respiration?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is the principal muscle of quiet inspiration.

questions.q: The Circle of Willis is located at the:
questions.explanation: The Circle of Willis is an arterial anastomosis at the base of the brain.

questions.q: Which blood vessel returns blood from the myocardium to the right atrium?
questions.explanation: Most cardiac venous drainage enters the right atrium via the coronary sinus.

questions.q: The islets of Langerhans are found in the:
questions.explanation: The islets of Langerhans are the endocrine portion of the pancreas.

questions.q: Which part of the small intestine is the longest?
questions.explanation: The ileum is the longest segment of the small intestine.

questions.q: The vocal cords are located in the:
questions.explanation: The vocal folds (cords) are within the larynx.

questions.q: Which bone is commonly called the collarbone?
questions.explanation: The clavicle is the collarbone.

questions.q: The glenohumeral joint is the:
questions.explanation: The glenohumeral joint is the ball-and-socket joint of the shoulder.

questions.q: Which structure produces cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?
questions.explanation: CSF is produced by the choroid plexus in the ventricles.

questions.q: The normal adult has how many pairs of spinal nerves?
questions.explanation: There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves.

questions.q: Which organ stores bile?
questions.explanation: Bile is produced by the liver and stored and concentrated in the gallbladder.

questions.q: The femur articulates distally with the:
questions.explanation: The distal femur articulates with the tibia and the patella.

questions.q: Which layer of the heart wall is the thickest?
questions.explanation: The myocardium (cardiac muscle) is the thickest layer.

questions.q: The optic nerve (CN II) exits the orbit via the:
questions.explanation: CN II passes through the optic canal.

questions.q: Which salivary gland is the largest?
questions.explanation: The parotid glands are the largest salivary glands.

questions.q: The appendix is attached to the:
questions.explanation: The vermiform appendix is attached to the caecum.

questions.q: Which vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood to the left atrium.

questions.q: The medulla oblongata is part of the:
questions.explanation: The brainstem comprises midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata.

questions.q: Which cartilage forms the Adam's apple?
questions.explanation: The laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple) is formed by the thyroid cartilage.

questions.q: The hip joint is an example of a:
questions.explanation: The hip is a ball-and-socket (spheroidal) synovial joint.

questions.q: Which structure filters blood in the kidney?
questions.explanation: The glomerulus is the capillary tuft where filtration occurs.

questions.q: The spleen is located in the:
questions.explanation: The spleen lies in the left upper quadrant under the diaphragm.

questions.q: Which nerve innervates the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve (C3–C5) innervates the diaphragm.

questions.q: The foramen ovale in the fetal heart connects the:
questions.explanation: In the fetus the foramen ovale allows blood to pass from right atrium to left atrium.

questions.q: Which bone contains the external auditory meatus?
questions.explanation: The external acoustic meatus is in the temporal bone.

questions.q: The thoracic duct drains lymph into the:
options: Left subclavian vein (near junction with internal jugular)
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct empties into the venous angle on the left side.

questions.q: Which part of the stomach is nearest the oesophagus?
questions.explanation: The cardia is the region around the oesophageal opening.

questions.q: The normal number of permanent teeth in an adult is:
questions.explanation: A complete adult dentition has 32 permanent teeth.

questions.q: Which meningeal layer is the outermost and toughest?
questions.explanation: The dura mater is the tough outer meningeal layer.

questions.q: The coronary arteries arise from the:
questions.explanation: The right and left coronary arteries originate from the ascending aorta just above the aortic valve.

questions.q: Which structure is known as the 'voice box'?
questions.explanation: The larynx houses the vocal cords and is commonly called the voice box.

questions.q: The olecranon is part of which bone?
questions.explanation: The olecranon is the proximal bony prominence of the ulna (the tip of the elbow).

questions.q: Which gland produces melatonin?
questions.explanation: The pineal gland secretes melatonin, which helps regulate sleep–wake cycles.

questions.q: The porta hepatis is found on the:
questions.explanation: The porta hepatis on the inferior liver surface transmits the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile ducts.

questions.q: Which spinal level is commonly used for lumbar puncture in adults?
questions.explanation: Lumbar puncture is performed below the termination of the spinal cord, typically at L3–L4 or L4–L5.

questions.q: The brachial artery is a continuation of the:
questions.explanation: The axillary artery becomes the brachial artery at the lower border of teres major.

questions.q: Which structure covers the lungs?
questions.explanation: The visceral and parietal pleura cover the lungs and line the thoracic cavity.

questions.q: The ischium, ilium and pubis together form the:
questions.explanation: Each hip bone is formed by the fusion of ilium, ischium and pubis.

questions.q: Which cranial nerve carries the sense of smell?
questions.explanation: CN I (olfactory) transmits smell.

questions.q: The ductus arteriosus in the fetus connects the:
questions.explanation: The ductus arteriosus shunts blood from the pulmonary trunk to the aorta, bypassing the lungs.

questions.q: Which organ has both endocrine and exocrine functions?
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes digestive enzymes (exocrine) and hormones such as insulin and glucagon (endocrine).

questions.q: The zygomatic bone is also called the:
questions.explanation: The zygomatic bone forms the prominence of the cheek.

questions.q: Which chamber has the thickest myocardial wall?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps against systemic resistance.

questions.q: The renal pyramids are located in the:
questions.explanation: The renal pyramids form the medulla of the kidney.

questions.q: Which nerve is compressed in carpal tunnel syndrome?
questions.explanation: The median nerve is compressed in the carpal tunnel.

questions.q: The epiglottis is composed mainly of:
questions.explanation: The epiglottis is elastic cartilage that covers the laryngeal inlet during swallowing.

questions.q: Which vessel is commonly used to measure blood pressure in the arm?
questions.explanation: Blood pressure is usually measured over the brachial artery.

questions.q: The corpus callosum connects the:
questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the major commissure linking the left and right cerebral hemispheres.

questions.q: Which structure is the site of fertilization in humans?
questions.explanation: Fertilization most often occurs in the ampulla of the uterine (fallopian) tube.

questions.q: The manubrium, body and xiphoid process are parts of the:
questions.explanation: These three parts make up the sternum.

questions.q: Which white blood cell is most abundant in normal peripheral blood?
questions.explanation: Neutrophils are the most numerous circulating leukocytes in healthy adults.

questions.q: The pituitary gland is suspended from the:
questions.explanation: The pituitary is attached to the hypothalamus by the pituitary stalk (infundibulum).

questions.q: Which bone does not articulate with any other bone?
questions.explanation: The hyoid bone is suspended by ligaments and muscles and does not form a joint with other bones.

questions.q: The pulmonary arteries carry:
questions.explanation: Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

questions.q: Which layer of the uterus is shed during menstruation?
questions.explanation: The functional layer of the endometrium is shed in menstruation.

questions.q: The cauda equina is found at the:
options: Lower end of the spinal cord
questions.explanation: Below the conus medullaris, lumbar and sacral nerve roots form the cauda equina.

questions.q: Which sinus is most commonly involved in sinusitis?
questions.explanation: The maxillary sinuses are the most frequently inflamed.

questions.q: The tendon of Achilles inserts into the:
questions.explanation: The Achilles (calcaneal) tendon inserts on the calcaneus.

questions.q: Which structure produces surfactant in the lung?
questions.explanation: Type II alveolar cells produce surfactant that reduces surface tension.

questions.q: The internal carotid artery enters the skull through the:
questions.explanation: The internal carotid artery ascends through the carotid canal in the temporal bone.

questions.q: Which part of the large intestine is S-shaped?
questions.explanation: The sigmoid colon is the S-shaped segment leading to the rectum.

questions.q: The sinoatrial node is located in the wall of the:
questions.explanation: The SA node lies in the upper wall of the right atrium near the superior vena cava.

questions.q: Which cranial nerve is tested by the pupillary light reflex (afferent limb)?
questions.explanation: The afferent limb of the pupillary light reflex is CN II; the efferent limb is CN III.

questions.q: The greater omentum is attached to the:
questions.explanation: The greater omentum hangs from the greater curvature of the stomach.

questions.q: Which bone forms the heel?
questions.explanation: The calcaneus is the heel bone.

questions.q: The tricuspid valve has how many cusps?
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve has three cusps.

questions.q: Which structure is the primary pacemaker if the SA node fails?
questions.explanation: The AV node can take over as a secondary pacemaker at a slower rate.

questions.q: The pleural cavity normally contains:
options: A small amount of lubricating fluid
questions.explanation: A thin film of pleural fluid allows the lungs to slide during respiration.

questions.q: Which artery is palpated in the neck to assess the pulse?
questions.explanation: The common carotid pulse is felt in the neck beside the trachea.

questions.q: The endometrium lines the:
questions.explanation: The endometrium is the inner lining of the uterus.

questions.q: Which structure closes the larynx during swallowing?
questions.explanation: The epiglottis folds back to cover the laryngeal inlet during swallowing.

questions.q: The radius is lateral to the ulna when the arm is in:
questions.explanation: In the anatomical position the radius is lateral and the ulna is medial.

questions.q: Which organ is both the largest gland and important for metabolism and detoxification?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest internal gland and has major metabolic and detoxifying roles.

questions.q: The spinal cord ends in adults approximately at the level of:
questions.explanation: In adults the spinal cord typically terminates at L1–L2.

questions.q: Which chamber receives blood from the pulmonary veins?
questions.explanation: The four pulmonary veins empty into the left atrium.

questions.q: The gallbladder is located on the:
options: Inferior surface of the right lobe of the liver
questions.explanation: The gallbladder sits in a fossa on the inferior surface of the right lobe of the liver.

questions.q: Which type of joint is the knee primarily?
questions.explanation: The knee is primarily a hinge joint (with some rotation when flexed).

questions.q: The auditory (Eustachian) tube connects the middle ear to the:
questions.explanation: The Eustachian tube equalises pressure between the middle ear and the nasopharynx.

questions.q: Which blood cells are responsible for oxygen transport?
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes (red blood cells) contain haemoglobin that carries oxygen.

questions.q: The normal resting heart rate in a healthy adult is approximately:
questions.explanation: Normal adult resting heart rate is typically 60–100 beats per minute.

questions.q: Oxygen is carried in the blood mainly by:
questions.explanation: About 97–98% of oxygen is transported bound to haemoglobin in red blood cells.

questions.q: The first heart sound (S1) is caused by:
questions.explanation: S1 is produced by closure of the mitral and tricuspid (AV) valves at the start of systole.

questions.q: Which hormone lowers blood glucose by promoting cellular uptake of glucose?
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake into cells and lowers blood glucose.

questions.q: The normal arterial blood pH range is:
questions.explanation: Normal arterial pH is 7.35–7.45.

questions.q: Which ion is most important for the resting membrane potential of nerves and muscle?
questions.explanation: The resting membrane potential depends largely on potassium conductance and the K+ concentration gradient.

questions.q: Surfactant in the alveoli functions to:
options: Reduce surface tension and prevent alveolar collapse
questions.explanation: Surfactant reduces surface tension, stabilising alveoli and preventing atelectasis.

questions.q: The primary stimulus for breathing under normal conditions is:
questions.explanation: Central chemoreceptors respond mainly to rising PaCO2 and the resulting fall in CSF pH.

questions.q: Which part of the nephron is impermeable to water in the absence of ADH?
options: Collecting duct only when ADH is present
questions.explanation: The thick ascending limb is impermeable to water; ADH acts on the collecting duct.

questions.q: Cardiac output equals:
questions.explanation: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate.

questions.q: The fight-or-flight response is mediated mainly by the:
questions.explanation: Sympathetic activation produces the fight-or-flight response.

questions.q: Which blood type is the universal donor for red cell transfusion (in basic ABO terms)?
questions.explanation: Group O negative red cells lack A, B and RhD antigens and are used as universal donor red cells in emergencies.

questions.q: ADH (vasopressin) primarily acts on the kidney to:
questions.explanation: ADH increases water permeability of the collecting ducts, concentrating the urine.

questions.q: The plateau phase of the cardiac action potential is mainly due to:
questions.explanation: The plateau is largely due to inward calcium current through L-type Ca2+ channels.

questions.q: Which enzyme converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II?
questions.explanation: ACE, mainly in the lung, converts angiotensin I to the active angiotensin II.

questions.q: Most carbon dioxide is transported in the blood as:
questions.explanation: About 70% of CO2 is transported as bicarbonate.

questions.q: The normal stroke volume of the adult heart is approximately:
questions.explanation: Typical resting stroke volume is about 70 mL.

questions.q: Which hormone is released from the posterior pituitary?
questions.explanation: The posterior pituitary releases ADH and oxytocin.

questions.q: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) in a healthy adult is approximately:
questions.explanation: Normal GFR is about 90–120 mL/min/1.73 m².

questions.q: The QRS complex on the ECG represents:
questions.explanation: The QRS complex corresponds to ventricular depolarisation.

questions.q: Parasympathetic stimulation of the heart causes:
questions.explanation: Vagal (parasympathetic) stimulation slows the heart rate.

questions.q: Which vitamin is required for clotting factor synthesis in the liver?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is needed for synthesis of factors II, VII, IX and X.

questions.q: Aldosterone mainly causes the kidney to:
questions.explanation: Aldosterone promotes sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion in the distal nephron.

questions.q: The oxygen–haemoglobin dissociation curve shifts to the right when there is:
options: Low CO2, low temperature, high pH
High CO2, high temperature, low pH
questions.explanation: A right shift (easier unloading of O2) occurs with increased CO2, temperature, 2,3-DPG and decreased pH.

questions.q: Which cells produce intrinsic factor?
questions.explanation: Parietal cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor (needed for B12 absorption).

questions.q: Starling's law of the heart states that:
options: Heart rate determines cardiac output alone
Stroke volume increases with increased end-diastolic fibre length (within limits)
Blood pressure is independent of venous return
questions.explanation: Within physiological limits, greater preload increases stroke volume (Frank–Starling mechanism).

questions.q: The main intracellular cation is:
questions.explanation: Potassium is the predominant cation inside cells; sodium is predominant outside.

questions.q: Which hormone raises blood calcium by increasing bone resorption and renal Ca2+ reabsorption?
questions.explanation: PTH increases serum calcium by effects on bone, kidney and (via vitamin D) gut.

questions.q: During exercise, blood flow to skeletal muscle:
questions.explanation: Local metabolites and neural mechanisms greatly increase muscle blood flow during exercise.

questions.q: The T wave on the ECG represents:
questions.explanation: The T wave corresponds to ventricular repolarisation.

questions.q: Which gas has the highest affinity for haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin with much higher affinity than oxygen.

questions.q: Renin is secreted by the:
questions.explanation: Juxtaglomerular cells release renin in response to low perfusion, low NaCl and sympathetic input.

questions.q: The main function of platelets is:
questions.explanation: Platelets are essential for primary haemostasis and plug formation.

questions.q: Which phase of the cardiac cycle is longer at normal heart rates?
questions.explanation: At rest, diastole lasts longer than systole.

questions.q: Thyroid hormones (T3/T4) primarily increase:
questions.explanation: Thyroid hormones raise basal metabolic rate and stimulate oxygen consumption.

questions.q: The gag reflex tests which cranial nerves?
questions.explanation: Afferent limb is mainly CN IX; efferent limb is CN X.

questions.q: Which buffer system is the most important in extracellular fluid?
questions.explanation: The bicarbonate–carbonic acid system is the primary ECF buffer.

questions.q: Erythropoietin is produced mainly by the:
questions.explanation: The kidneys produce most erythropoietin in response to hypoxia.

questions.q: The absolute refractory period in cardiac muscle:
options: Is shorter than in skeletal muscle
questions.explanation: A long refractory period prevents tetanic contraction and permits diastolic filling.

questions.q: Which immunoglobulin is the most abundant in serum?
questions.explanation: IgG is the predominant circulating antibody.

questions.q: Mean arterial pressure is approximately:
questions.explanation: MAP ≈ diastolic pressure + one-third of pulse pressure.

questions.q: Which structure detects changes in blood pressure in the carotid sinus?
questions.explanation: Baroreceptors in the carotid sinus and aortic arch sense stretch (pressure).

questions.q: Insulin is secreted by which pancreatic cells?
questions.explanation: Beta cells of the islets secrete insulin.

questions.q: The primary purpose of the urea cycle is to:
questions.explanation: The urea cycle converts toxic ammonia into urea for excretion.

questions.q: Which ion enters the neuron during the upstroke of the action potential?
questions.explanation: Rapid sodium influx causes the depolarising phase of the neuronal action potential.

questions.q: Haematocrit is the:
options: Percentage of blood volume occupied by red cells
Amount of haemoglobin per red cell
questions.explanation: Haematocrit is the packed cell volume (fraction of blood that is erythrocytes).

questions.q: Which hormone is responsible for milk ejection?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin causes contraction of myoepithelial cells and milk let-down.

questions.q: The normal adult respiratory rate at rest is approximately:
questions.explanation: Resting respiratory rate in adults is typically 12–20 breaths per minute.

questions.q: Which factor increases oxygen unloading in tissues?
questions.explanation: Acidosis, raised temperature and 2,3-DPG shift the O2 curve to the right, aiding unloading.

questions.q: The main site of nutrient absorption is the:
questions.explanation: Most digestion and absorption of nutrients occur in the small intestine.

questions.q: Sympathetic stimulation of the bronchi causes:
questions.explanation: Beta-2 sympathetic stimulation relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.

questions.q: Which plasma protein is most important for maintaining oncotic pressure?
questions.explanation: Albumin is the major contributor to plasma colloid osmotic (oncotic) pressure.

questions.q: The PR interval on the ECG represents:
options: Time from atrial to ventricular depolarisation (including AV delay)
questions.explanation: The PR interval reflects conduction from atria through the AV node to the ventricles.

questions.q: Which hormone stimulates gastric acid secretion?
questions.explanation: Gastrin stimulates parietal cells to secrete HCl.

questions.q: In metabolic acidosis the respiratory compensation is:
questions.explanation: Hyperventilation lowers PaCO2 and helps raise pH toward normal.

questions.q: The normal fasting blood glucose range is approximately:
questions.explanation: Typical fasting plasma glucose is about 3.5–5.5 mmol/L (lab ranges vary slightly).

questions.q: Which cells are the first line of cellular defence against bacteria?
questions.explanation: Neutrophils are rapid phagocytes that form the first cellular response to most bacteria.

questions.q: Stroke volume decreases when:
questions.explanation: High afterload makes it harder to eject blood and can reduce stroke volume.

questions.q: The hormone that stimulates red blood cell production is:
questions.explanation: Erythropoietin stimulates erythropoiesis in the bone marrow.

questions.q: Which phase of swallowing is under voluntary control?
questions.explanation: The oral phase is voluntary; pharyngeal and oesophageal phases are reflex.

questions.q: Calcitonin is produced by the:
questions.explanation: Thyroid C (parafollicular) cells secrete calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium.

questions.q: The main intracellular anion is:
questions.explanation: Organic phosphates and proteins are the major intracellular anions.

questions.q: Which factor initiates the intrinsic pathway of coagulation?
questions.explanation: The intrinsic pathway begins with contact activation involving factor XII.

questions.q: Venous return increases when:
options: Person stands still for a long time
questions.explanation: Muscle contraction compresses veins and aids return of blood to the heart.

questions.q: The normal adult blood volume is approximately:
questions.explanation: Adult blood volume is roughly 5 litres (about 70 mL/kg).

questions.q: Which receptor type is activated by acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction?
questions.explanation: Nicotinic ACh receptors mediate transmission at the skeletal neuromuscular junction.

questions.q: Respiratory alkalosis is caused by:
questions.explanation: Hyperventilation blows off CO2, raising pH (respiratory alkalosis).

questions.q: The main site of action of loop diuretics is the:
options: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle
questions.explanation: Loop diuretics inhibit the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb.

questions.q: Which statement about fetal haemoglobin (HbF) is correct?
options: It binds 2,3-DPG more tightly than HbA
It has higher affinity for oxygen than adult Hb
It is the main haemoglobin after age 5 years
questions.explanation: HbF has higher O2 affinity, facilitating oxygen transfer from mother to fetus.

questions.q: The Bainbridge reflex is triggered by:
questions.explanation: Atrial stretch from increased venous return can increase heart rate (Bainbridge reflex).

questions.q: Which enzyme breaks down acetylcholine in the synaptic cleft?
questions.explanation: Acetylcholinesterase rapidly hydrolyses ACh, ending transmission.

questions.q: In the proximal tubule, most filtered glucose is reabsorbed by:
questions.explanation: Sodium–glucose linked transporters (SGLT) reabsorb glucose in the proximal tubule.

questions.q: Which hormone peaks just before ovulation and triggers it?
questions.explanation: The mid-cycle LH surge triggers ovulation.

questions.q: Dead space in the respiratory system is the volume of air that:
options: Reaches the alveoli and exchanges gas
Does not participate in gas exchange
questions.explanation: Anatomical dead space is the conducting airway volume where no gas exchange occurs.

questions.q: The main cation in extracellular fluid is:
questions.explanation: Sodium is the principal extracellular cation.

questions.q: Which statement about the action potential in skeletal muscle is true?
options: It lasts as long as cardiac muscle
It is much shorter than in cardiac muscle
It has a long plateau due to calcium
It does not involve sodium channels
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle action potentials are brief; cardiac ones have a long plateau.

questions.q: Secretin stimulates the pancreas to release:
questions.explanation: Secretin causes the pancreas to secrete bicarbonate-rich juice to neutralise duodenal acid.

questions.q: Which factor decreases haemoglobin's affinity for oxygen (right shift)?
questions.explanation: Acidosis reduces Hb–O2 affinity (Bohr effect), facilitating unloading.

questions.q: The primary pacemaker of the heart depolarises spontaneously because of:
questions.explanation: Pacemaker cells have spontaneous diastolic depolarisation driven by If and calcium currents.

questions.q: Which vitamin deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia due to impaired DNA synthesis?
questions.explanation: B12 and folate are required for DNA synthesis; deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia.

questions.q: Compliance of the lung is reduced in:
questions.explanation: Fibrosis stiffens the lung and reduces compliance.

questions.q: The intrinsic rate of the AV node is approximately:
questions.explanation: If the SA node fails, the AV node can pace at about 40–60 beats/min.

questions.q: Which process describes water movement across a semi-permeable membrane due to solute concentration?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the net movement of water toward higher solute concentration.

questions.q: Cortisol is produced in the:
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids such as cortisol are synthesised in the zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex.

questions.q: The main force driving glomerular filtration is:
options: Hydrostatic pressure in the glomerular capillaries
questions.explanation: Glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure is the primary driving force for filtration.

questions.q: Which lipoprotein carries cholesterol from the liver to peripheral tissues?
questions.explanation: LDL transports cholesterol to tissues; elevated LDL is associated with atherosclerosis.

questions.q: During isovolumetric contraction of the left ventricle:
options: Both AV and aortic valves are closed
questions.explanation: Isovolumetric contraction occurs with all valves closed until ventricular pressure exceeds aortic pressure.

questions.q: Which neurotransmitter is deficient in Parkinson's disease?
questions.explanation: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra causes Parkinsonian features.

questions.q: The Hering–Breuer reflex is triggered by:
questions.explanation: Stretch receptors in the lung mediate the Hering–Breuer inflation reflex.

questions.q: Which ion is essential for excitation–contraction coupling in skeletal muscle?
questions.explanation: Calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum initiates contraction.

questions.q: Plasma oncotic pressure opposes:
questions.explanation: Oncotic pressure pulls fluid into the capillary and opposes filtration.

questions.q: Which hormone increases basal metabolic rate and is essential for normal growth and development?
questions.explanation: Thyroid hormones regulate metabolic rate and are critical for growth and CNS development.

questions.q: The normal ratio of bicarbonate to carbonic acid in blood is approximately:
questions.explanation: The normal HCO3− : H2CO3 ratio is about 20:1, which maintains pH near 7.4.

questions.q: Which statement about smooth muscle is correct?
options: It lacks sarcomeres and is involuntary
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle is non-striated and involuntary.

questions.q: The main site of ADH action is the:
questions.explanation: ADH inserts aquaporins in the collecting duct epithelium.

questions.q: Which blood component is primarily responsible for humoral immunity?
questions.explanation: B cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies.

questions.q: Afterload is best described as:
options: The pressure the ventricle must overcome to eject blood
questions.explanation: Afterload is the load against which the ventricle contracts (approximated by aortic pressure).

questions.q: Which condition shifts the oxygen–haemoglobin curve to the left?
questions.explanation: Left shift (higher affinity, less unloading) occurs with alkalosis, hypothermia and low 2,3-DPG.

questions.q: The functional residual capacity (FRC) is the volume of air:
questions.explanation: FRC is the volume left in the lungs after a normal tidal expiration.

questions.q: Which process requires ATP at the carrier protein itself?
questions.explanation: Primary active transport uses ATP directly (e.g. Na+/K+ ATPase).
